agencies.name: National Environment Agency (NEA)
agencies.role: Computes and publishes the 24-hour PSI and 1-hour PM2.5 for five regions, issues haze situation updates and forecasts.

agencies.name: Ministry of Health (MOH)
agencies.role: Publishes health advisories tied to the 24-hour PSI forecast and the 1-hour PM2.5 bands, including mask guidance.

agencies.name: Meteorological Service Singapore (MSS)
agencies.role: Publishes weather and haze outlooks and an archive on transboundary smoke haze episodes.

agencies.name: Haze Task Force
agencies.role: Inter-agency body formed in 1994 to coordinate government action on haze.

nationalIndex.name: Pollutant Standards Index (24-hour PSI)
nationalIndex.description: Computed from 24-hour averages of six pollutants (PM10, PM2.5, SO2, NO2, O3 and CO). Each pollutant gets a sub-index and the highest becomes the PSI. Bands: 0–50 Good, 51–100 Moderate, 101–200 Unhealthy, 201–300 Very Unhealthy, above 300 Hazardous.

monitoring.text: NEA publishes the 24-hour PSI on a rolling basis and 1-hour PM2.5 readings every hour for the North, South, East, West and Central regions.
PM2.5 became the sixth pollutant in the 24-hour PSI in April 2014, and NEA began publishing hourly PM2.5 readings that year. Bands for the 1-hour PM2.5 were introduced in 2016.
NEA says other sites such as aqicn.org use different computation methods, so their readings are not comparable with the 24-hour PSI.

seasonalPattern.text: MSS describes the major 1997 haze as occurring during the Southwest Monsoon, August to October, easing with the Northeast Monsoon in November.
In recent episodes NEA has linked haze arrivals to southeasterly winds carrying smoke from Kalimantan and southwesterly winds from Sumatra.
During the Northeast Monsoon, winds from the north-west and north-east can carry smoke from mainland Southeast Asia, as in March 2025.

healthContext.text: MOH advice differs for healthy people, for the elderly, pregnant women and children, and for people with chronic lung or heart disease. At 24-hour PSI 101–200, healthy people should reduce prolonged or strenuous outdoor exertion.
MOH says N95 masks are not needed for commuting or indoors, and recommends one for the general public when PM2.5 is above 250 µg/m³ and they must be outdoors for several hours.

policy.text: The Transboundary Haze Pollution Act 2014 applies to conduct outside Singapore that causes or contributes to haze pollution in Singapore, defined by a poor air quality episode lasting at least 24 hours.
The Haze Task Force was formed to coordinate government action.

dataAccess.name: data.gov.sg real-time API (PSI, PM2.5, weather)
dataAccess.note: Public, no key required (optional key raises the rate limit), Singapore Open Data Licence v1.0. Connected on this platform.

dataAccess.name: haze.gov.sg historical readings
dataAccess.note: Web table for the past year behind a captcha. NEA points to data.gov.sg for older data.

openQuestions: NEA's archive is published monthly, so the most recent weeks rely on the live API until the next batch appears.
